original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-nonzero-some-cohomology}
Let $X$ be a scheme and $\mathcal{L}$ an ample invertible
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module. If $K$ is a nonzero object of
$D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)$, then for some $n \geq 0$ and $p \in \mathbf{Z}$
the cohomology group
$H^p(X, K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{L}^{\otimes n})$
is nonzero.
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and $\mathcal{L}$ an ample invertible
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module. If $K$ is a nonzero object of
$D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)$, then for some $n \geq 0$ and $p \in \mathbf{Z}$
the cohomology group
$H^p(X, K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{L}^{\otimes n})$
is nonzero.
hypotheses: X is scheme; L is AMPLE invertible O_X-module.
conclusions: There exist n≥0 and p∈ℤ such that H^p(X,K⊗^L L^⊗n) ≠0.
semantic_review_note: Joint choice of n and p is existential for the given nonzero K; n nonnegative, not arbitrary negative twists.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-construct-the-next-one}
Let $A$ be a ring. Let $X = \mathbf{P}^n_A$. For every $a \in \mathbf{Z}$
there exists an exact complex
$$
0 \to \mathcal{O}_X(a) \to \ldots
\to \mathcal{O}_X(a + i)^{\oplus {n + 1 \choose i}} \to
\ldots \to \mathcal{O}_X(a + n + 1) \to 0
$$
of vector bundles on $X$.
statement:
Let $A$ be a ring. Let $X = \mathbf{P}^n_A$. For every $a \in \mathbf{Z}$
there exists an exact complex
$$
0 \to \mathcal{O}_X(a) \to \ldots
\to \mathcal{O}_X(a + i)^{\oplus {n + 1 \choose i}} \to
\ldots \to \mathcal{O}_X(a + n + 1) \to 0
$$
of vector bundles on $X$.
hypotheses: A is ring, n≥0 integer, X=ℙ^n_A.
conclusions: There exists an EXACT complex of vector bundles 0→O_X(a)→⋯→O_X(a+i)^⊕(binom(n+1,i))→⋯→O_X(a+n+1)→0.
semantic_review_note: Exactness of full vector bundle complex, with n+1 steps and binomial multiplicities. Do not assert a preferred canonical differential without source.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-generator-P1}
Let $A$ be a ring. Let $X = \mathbf{P}^n_A$. Then
$$
E =
\mathcal{O}_X \oplus \mathcal{O}_X(-1) \oplus \ldots \oplus \mathcal{O}_X(-n)
$$
is a generator
(Derived Categories, Definition \ref{derived-definition-generators})
of $D_\QCoh(X)$.
statement:
Let $A$ be a ring. Let $X = \mathbf{P}^n_A$. Then
$$
E =
\mathcal{O}_X \oplus \mathcal{O}_X(-1) \oplus \ldots \oplus \mathcal{O}_X(-n)
$$
is a generator
(Derived Categories, Definition \ref{derived-definition-generators})
of $D_\QCoh(X)$.
conclusions: The SINGLE perfect object E=⊕_(i=0..n) O_X(-i) generates D_QCoh(X) in the triangulated/localizing sense.
semantic_review_note: One direct sum is a generator, not each summand individually; includes n=0 case.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-compact-is-perfect}
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
An object of $D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)$ is compact
if and only if it is perfect.
statement:
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
An object of $D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)$ is compact
if and only if it is perfect.
conclusions: E is compact in D_QCoh(O_X) iff E is perfect as a complex of O_X-modules.
equivalence_sides: E is compact in D_QCoh(O_X) iff E is perfect as a complex of O_X-modules.
semantic_review_note: Compactness means Hom(E,-) commutes with arbitrary direct sums; no coherence or Noetherian hypothesis.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-compact-is-perfect-with-support}
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Let $T \subset X$ be a closed subset such that $X \setminus T$
is quasi-compact. An object of $D_{\QCoh, T}(\mathcal{O}_X)$ is compact
if and only if it is perfect as an object of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
statement:
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Let $T \subset X$ be a closed subset such that $X \setminus T$
is quasi-compact. An object of $D_{\QCoh, T}(\mathcal{O}_X)$ is compact
if and only if it is perfect as an object of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
conclusions: E is compact in the supported derived subcategory iff E is PERFECT as object of D(O_X).
equivalence_sides: E is compact in the supported derived subcategory iff E is PERFECT as object of D(O_X).
semantic_review_note: Compactness must be measured in D_(QCoh,T), not unrestricted D_QCoh(X), and support premise retained.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-map-from-pseudo-coherent-to-complex-with-support}
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Let $T \subset X$
be a closed subset such that $U = X \setminus T$ is quasi-compact.
Let $\alpha : P \to E$ be a morphism of $D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)$ with
either
\begin{enumerate}
\item $P$ is perfect and $E$ supported on $T$, or
\item $P$ pseudo-coherent, $E$ supported on $T$, and $E$ bounded below.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a perfect complex of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules $I$
and a map $I \to \mathcal{O}_X[0]$ such that
$I \otimes^\mathbf{L} P \to E$ is zero and such that
$I|_U \to \mathcal{O}_U[0]$ is an
isomorphism.
statement:
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Let $T \subset X$
be a closed subset such that $U = X \setminus T$ is quasi-compact.
Let $\alpha : P \to E$ be a morphism of $D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)$ with
either
\begin{enumerate}
\item $P$ is perfect and $E$ supported on $T$, or
\item $P$ pseudo-coherent, $E$ supported on $T$, and $E$ bounded below.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a perfect complex of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules $I$
and a map $I \to \mathcal{O}_X[0]$ such that
$I \otimes^\mathbf{L} P \to E$ is zero and such that
$I|_U \to \mathcal{O}_U[0]$ is an
isomorphism.
hypotheses: T⊂X closed with quasi-compact complement U.
E is supported T and EITHER P perfect OR (P pseudo-coherent AND E bounded below).
conclusions: There exist a perfect I on X and map I→O_X such that I⊗^L P→E, induced by α, is ZERO.
The restriction I|U→O_U is an ISOMORPHISM.
semantic_review_note: Two alternative premise branches with shared E-support guard; a single I→O_X meets BOTH conclusions.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-tensor-with-QCoh-complex}
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $K^\bullet$ be a complex of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
whose cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent. Let
$(E, d) = \Hom_{\text{Comp}^{dg}(\mathcal{O}_X)}(K^\bullet, K^\bullet)$
be the endomorphism differential graded algebra. Then the functor
$$
- \otimes_E^\mathbf{L} K^\bullet :
D(E, \text{d}) \longrightarrow D(\mathcal{O}_X)
$$
of
Differential Graded Algebra, Lemma
\ref{dga-lemma-tensor-with-complex-derived}
has image contained in $D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)$.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{theorem-DQCoh-is-Ddga}
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Then there exist a differential graded algebra $(E, \text{d})$
with only a finite number of nonzero cohomology groups $H^i(E)$
such that $D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)$ is equivalent
to $D(E, \text{d})$.
statement:
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Then there exist a differential graded algebra $(E, \text{d})$
with only a finite number of nonzero cohomology groups $H^i(E)$
such that $D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)$ is equivalent
to $D(E, \text{d})$.
conclusions: There exists a differential graded algebra (E,d) with ONLY FINITELY MANY nonzero H^i(E) such that D_QCoh(O_X)≃D(E,d).
semantic_review_note: One dg algebra giving derived-category equivalence; finite number of cohomology DEGREES (not each H^i finite rank).

semantic_review_note: Two equivalent statements; one coherent compatible system K_n for all n, not one isolated approximation per n.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-pseudo-coherent-hocolim-with-support}
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Let $T \subset X$ be a closed subset such that $X \setminus T$
is quasi-compact. Let $K \in D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ supported on $T$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $K$ is pseudo-coherent, and
\item $K = \text{hocolim} K_n$ where
$K_n$ is perfect, supported on $T$, and
$\tau_{\geq -n}K_n \to \tau_{\geq -n}K$ is an isomorphism for all $n$.
\end{enumerate}
